name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER_9_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Specific enzymes used for cell wall digestion

questiontext.text:
Match the enzymes listed in List I with their corresponding target cells or molecules in List II:

List I List II
A. Lysozyme I. Breaks fungal cell wall
B. Cellulase II. Removes RNA from cellular extract
C. Chitinase III. Breaks bacterial cell wall
D. Ribonuclease IV. Breaks plant cell wall

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the catalytic function of each lytic enzyme:
• Lysozyme specifically degrades the peptidoglycan cell wall of bacteria to release intracellular contents.
• Cellulase hydrolyzes cellulose present in the rigid cell wall of plant cells.
• Chitinase catalyzes the degradation of chitin, the structural polysaccharide found in fungal cell walls.
• Ribonuclease digests RNA molecules present in the cellular lysate to ensure isolation of purified DNA.

Step 2: Establish the correct conceptual pairings:
• Lysozyme pairs with breaking bacterial cell wall.
• Cellulase pairs with breaking plant cell wall.
• Chitinase pairs with breaking fungal cell wall.
• Ribonuclease pairs with removing RNA from cellular extract.

Step 3: State the final answer:
Combining these pairs gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER_9_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Key steps and components of polymerase chain reaction

questiontext.text:
Match the stages and components of Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. Denaturation I. Binding of oligonucleotide primers to complementary regions of DNA
B. Annealing II. Thermostable DNA polymerase isolated from Thermus aquaticus
C. Extension III. Separation of double-stranded DNA into single strands by heat
D. Taq polymerase IV. Synthesis of complementary DNA strand using deoxynucleotides

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the thermal steps and enzymatic role in PCR:
• Denaturation is the initial step where high temperature induces unwinding and separation of double-stranded DNA into two single template strands.
• Annealing involves cooling to allow small chemically synthesised oligonucleotide primers to hybridize to their complementary regions on the single-stranded DNA.
• Extension involves synthesis of the new DNA strand complementary to the template strand by the addition of deoxynucleotides.
• Taq polymerase is a thermostable DNA polymerase isolated from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus that remains active during the high-temperature denaturation step.

Step 2: Establish the correct conceptual pairings:
• Denaturation pairs with separation of double-stranded DNA into single strands by heat.
• Annealing pairs with binding of oligonucleotide primers to complementary regions of DNA.
• Extension pairs with synthesis of complementary DNA strand using deoxynucleotides.
• Taq polymerase pairs with thermostable DNA polymerase isolated from Thermus aquaticus.

Step 3: State the final answer:
Combining these pairs gives A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER_9_MATCHING_MCQ_Q03 - Scientists and major milestones in recombinant biotechnology

questiontext.text:
Match the scientists and historical milestones in List I with their major scientific contributions in List II:

List I List II
A. Herbert Boyer I. Developed methods of isolating native bacterial plasmids and reinserting them
B. Stanley Cohen II. Characterization of the first sequence-specific restriction endonuclease cutting at six base pairs
C. European Federation of Biotechnology III. Discovered restriction enzymes producing 'sticky ends' in E. coli
D. Isolation of Hind II IV. Formulated a definition encompassing traditional and modern molecular biotechnology

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the historical contribution of each scientist and milestone:
• Herbert Boyer observed in 1969 that certain restriction enzymes of Escherichia coli cut DNA in a staggered fashion leaving cohesive single-stranded 'sticky ends'.
• Stanley Cohen developed methods of removing circular extrachromosomal plasmids from bacterial cells and reintroducing them into other bacterial cells.
• The European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB) provided a unifying definition: "The integration of natural science and organisms, cells, parts thereof, and molecular analogues for products and services."
• The first restriction endonuclease whose functioning depended on a specific nucleotide recognition sequence was Hind II, isolated and characterized to cut at a specific sequence of six base pairs.

Step 2: Establish the correct conceptual pairings:
• Herbert Boyer pairs with discovering restriction enzymes producing sticky ends in E. coli.
• Stanley Cohen pairs with developing methods of isolating native plasmids and reinserting them.
• European Federation of Biotechnology pairs with formulating a definition encompassing traditional and modern molecular biotechnology.
• Isolation of Hind II pairs with characterization of the first sequence-specific restriction endonuclease cutting at six base pairs.

Step 3: State the final answer:
Combining these pairs gives A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER_9_MATCHING_MCQ_Q04 - Essential functional features of plasmid cloning vectors

questiontext.text:
Match the essential vector features in List I with their primary functional roles in List II:

List I List II
A. Origin of replication (ori) I. Codes for proteins involved in plasmid replication
B. rop gene II. Identifies and eliminates non-transformants while permitting transformant growth
C. Selectable marker III. Initiates replication and controls the copy number of linked foreign DNA
D. Unique cloning site IV. Prevents generation of multiple DNA fragments that complicate gene cloning

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the functional significance of vector components:
• The origin of replication (ori) is the specific DNA sequence where replication originates; it is also responsible for controlling the copy number of the cloned gene.
• The rop gene encodes the repressor of primer proteins, which are directly involved in controlling the replication of the plasmid.
• A selectable marker helps in identifying transformants and selectively eliminating non-transformants (such as antibiotic resistance genes in E. coli).
• A single (unique) cloning site ensures that the restriction enzyme makes a single cut; having multiple recognition sites would cut the vector into several fragments, complicating the cloning process.

Step 2: Establish the correct conceptual pairings:
• Origin of replication pairs with initiating replication and controlling the copy number of linked foreign DNA.
• rop gene pairs with coding for proteins involved in plasmid replication.
• Selectable marker pairs with identifying and eliminating non-transformants while permitting transformant growth.
• Unique cloning site pairs with preventing generation of multiple DNA fragments that complicate gene cloning.

Step 3: State the final answer:
Combining these pairs gives A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER_9_MATCHING_MCQ_Q05 - Gene transfer methods into competent host cells

questiontext.text:
Match the gene transfer methods in List I with their corresponding principles and applications in List II:

List I List II
A. Micro-injection I. High-velocity bombardment with DNA-coated gold or tungsten micro-particles
B. Biolistics II. Divalent cation treatment followed by heat shock at 42°C
C. Chemical competency III. Non-pathogenic natural vehicles delivering recombinant genes into eukaryotic cells
D. Disarmed pathogen vectors IV. Direct delivery of recombinant DNA into the nucleus of an animal cell

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review the mechanism of each gene introduction method:
• Micro-injection is a technique where recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell using a specialized micro-needle.
• Biolistics (gene gun) involves bombarding plant cells with high-velocity microscopic particles of heavy metals such as gold or tungsten coated with foreign DNA.
• Chemical competency involves treating bacterial cells with a divalent cation such as calcium to increase cell wall permeability, followed by an ice-heat shock (42°C)-ice cycle.
• Disarmed pathogen vectors (such as modified Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumifaciens or disarmed retroviruses) exploit natural viral or bacterial infection pathways to transfer genes without causing disease.

Step 2: Establish the correct conceptual pairings:
• Micro-injection pairs with direct delivery of recombinant DNA into the nucleus of an animal cell.
• Biolistics pairs with high-velocity bombardment with DNA-coated gold or tungsten micro-particles.
• Chemical competency pairs with divalent cation treatment followed by heat shock at 42°C.
• Disarmed pathogen vectors pairs with non-pathogenic natural vehicles delivering recombinant genes into eukaryotic cells.

Step 3: State the final answer:
Combining these pairs gives A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER_9_MATCHING_MCQ_Q06 - Nomenclature conventions of restriction endonuclease enzymes

questiontext.text:
Match the components of the restriction enzyme designation EcoRI in List I with their taxonomic or isolation origins in List II:

List I List II
A. First letter 'E' I. Represents the species name coli
B. Next two letters 'co' II. Represents the strain RY 13
C. Letter 'R' III. Indicates the chronological order of isolation from that strain
D. Roman numeral 'I' IV. Represents the genus name Escherichia

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the standard nomenclature rules for restriction endonucleases:
• The first capital letter is derived from the first letter of the bacterial genus (for EcoRI, 'E' stands for Escherichia).
• The next two lowercase letters come from the first two letters of the bacterial species (for EcoRI, 'co' stands for coli).
• The fourth letter represents the specific bacterial strain from which the enzyme was purified (for EcoRI, 'R' stands for strain RY 13).
• The Roman numerals following the letters denote the sequential order in which the restriction enzyme was isolated from that particular strain of bacteria.

Step 2: Establish the correct conceptual pairings:
• First letter 'E' pairs with representing the genus name Escherichia.
• Next two letters 'co' pair with representing the species name coli.
• Letter 'R' pairs with representing the strain RY 13.
• Roman numeral 'I' pairs with indicating the chronological order of isolation from that strain.

Step 3: State the final answer:
Combining these pairs gives A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER_9_MATCHING_MCQ_Q07 - Separation and visualization in agarose gel electrophoresis

questiontext.text:
Match the terms associated with agarose gel electrophoresis in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. Agarose I. Intercalating dye required to stain separated DNA fragments
B. Ethidium bromide II. Cutting out and extracting resolved DNA bands from the gel slice
C. Ultraviolet (UV) light III. Natural polymer from seaweeds providing a sieving matrix
D. Elution IV. Radiation necessary to visualize bright orange-colored DNA bands

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand each stage and reagent used in agarose gel electrophoresis:
• Agarose is a natural polysaccharide extracted from seaweeds that polymerizes into a gel matrix, providing a sieving effect to resolve DNA fragments according to molecular size.
• Ethidium bromide is an intercalating fluorescent stain used to bind DNA because pure nucleic acids cannot be seen under visible light.
• Exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation excites ethidium bromide intercalated into DNA, causing it to emit visible bright orange fluorescence.
• Elution is the process of cutting out the desired separated band of DNA from the agarose gel slab and chemically extracting it from the gel slice for further cloning steps.

Step 2: Establish the correct conceptual pairings:
• Agarose pairs with natural polymer from seaweeds providing a sieving matrix.
• Ethidium bromide pairs with intercalating dye required to stain separated DNA fragments.
• Ultraviolet light pairs with radiation necessary to visualize bright orange-colored DNA bands.
• Elution pairs with cutting out and extracting resolved DNA bands from the gel slice.

Step 3: State the final answer:
Combining these pairs gives A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER_9_MATCHING_MCQ_Q08 - Restriction endonuclease recognition sites in plasmid pBR322

questiontext.text:
Match the restriction enzymes in List I with their precise location/gene harboring them in cloning vector pBR322 in List II:

List I List II
A. BamHI I. Within the ampicillin resistance gene (ampR)
B. PstI II. Within the rop gene coding sequence
C. EcoRI III. Within the tetracycline resistance gene (tetR)
D. PvuII IV. Outside antibiotic resistance genes and rop region

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the restriction map of cloning vector pBR322:
• In pBR322, the tetracycline resistance gene (tetR) contains recognition sites for BamHI and SalI.
• The ampicillin resistance gene (ampR) carries recognition sites for PstI and PvuI.
• The rop gene (which encodes proteins involved in plasmid replication) contains the recognition site for PvuII.
• The cloning sites for EcoRI, ClaI, and HindIII are located in the intergenic region outside the antibiotic resistance markers and rop.

Step 2: Establish the correct conceptual pairings:
• BamHI pairs with within the tetracycline resistance gene.
• PstI pairs with within the ampicillin resistance gene.
• EcoRI pairs with outside antibiotic resistance genes and rop region.
• PvuII pairs with within the rop gene coding sequence.

Step 3: State the final answer:
Combining these pairs gives A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER_9_MATCHING_MCQ_Q09 - Selectable markers and insertional inactivation screening methods

questiontext.text:
Match the genetic processes and biotechnological techniques in List I with their corresponding diagnostic outcomes in List II:

List I List II
A. Insertion at BamHI site of pBR322 I. White recombinant colonies and blue non-recombinant colonies on chromogenic substrate
B. Insertion within β-galactosidase coding sequence II. Maintenance of cells in physiologically active log/exponential phase by continuous medium exchange
C. Continuous culture system III. Transformants grow on ampicillin medium but fail to grow on tetracycline medium
D. Downstream processing IV. Sequential product separation, purification, preservation, and clinical trials

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the biochemical principle of each process:
• Ligation of a foreign gene at the BamHI site of pBR322 disrupts the tetracycline resistance gene (insertional inactivation of tetR); recombinants retain ampicillin resistance and grow on ampicillin plates, but lose tetracycline resistance and cannot grow on tetracycline plates.
• Insertion of foreign DNA into the coding sequence of β-galactosidase (lacZ) results in insertional inactivation of the enzyme; non-recombinant cells form blue colonies in the presence of a chromogenic substrate (X-gal), whereas recombinants form colorless/white colonies.
• In a continuous culture system, nutrient medium is continuously refreshed from one end while spent medium is removed from the other, sustaining microorganisms at their peak exponential (log) growth phase for optimal protein biomass accumulation.
• Downstream processing encompasses all post-biosynthetic stages, including product separation, purification, stabilization with preservatives, and stringent quality control/clinical testing.

Step 2: Establish the correct conceptual pairings:
• Insertion at BamHI site of pBR322 pairs with transformants growing on ampicillin medium but failing to grow on tetracycline medium.
• Insertion within β-galactosidase coding sequence pairs with white recombinant colonies and blue non-recombinant colonies on chromogenic substrate.
• Continuous culture system pairs with maintenance of cells in physiologically active log/exponential phase by continuous medium exchange.
• Downstream processing pairs with sequential product separation, purification, preservation, and clinical trials.

Step 3: State the final answer:
Combining these pairs gives A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER_9_MATCHING_MCQ_Q10 - Structural components and functions of stirred bioreactors

questiontext.text:
Match the structural components of a stirred-tank bioreactor in List I with their precise functional roles in List II:

List I List II
A. Curved reactor base I. Enables periodic withdrawal of small culture volumes for testing
B. Flat-bladed impeller agitator II. Ensures even mixing and uniform oxygen availability throughout the culture broth
C. Sparger system III. Introduces sterile air bubbles to dramatically increase surface area for oxygen transfer
D. Sampling port IV. Prevents stagnation and facilitates smooth circular mixing of the reactor contents

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the engineering features of stirred-tank bioreactors:
• The curved (hemispherical) base of the vessel is engineered specifically to eliminate dead zones and facilitate smooth hydrodynamic mixing of the culture broth.
• The flat-bladed impeller driven by an overhead motor facilitates uniform stirring, distribution of nutrients, and homogeneous oxygen availability throughout the entire volume.
• The sparger system introduces sterile compressed air as micro-bubbles into the liquid medium, which dramatically increases the interfacial surface area for gas transfer.
• The sampling port allows sterile extraction of small culture aliquots at regular intervals to monitor microbial growth, substrate utilization, and product concentration without interrupting the process.

Step 2: Establish the correct conceptual pairings:
• Curved reactor base pairs with preventing stagnation and facilitating smooth circular mixing of the reactor contents.
• Flat-bladed impeller agitator pairs with ensuring even mixing and uniform oxygen availability throughout the culture broth.
• Sparger system pairs with introducing sterile air bubbles to dramatically increase surface area for oxygen transfer.
• Sampling port pairs with enabling periodic withdrawal of small culture volumes for testing.

Step 3: State the final answer:
Combining these pairs gives A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I.
